extraction.agency_name: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
extraction.parent_department: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene

findings.title: Potential Risks of the MERP Project and Key Aspects of the Procurement Process Were Not Formally Disclosed to BPW
findings.description: DHMH did not formally communicate certain pertinent aspects of the MERP procurement process and potential risks regarding the award decision when it sought Board of Public Works approval. There was a lack of evidence that the BPW or its staff were fully apprised of RFP qualification changes, past performance issues of the successful bidder, or changes to contractor liability provisions.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that, in the future, DHMH ensure that all pertinent circumstances regarding significant procurement award decisions, including potential risks, are clearly documented and conveyed to BPW for its consideration of contracts submitted for approval.

findings.title: The LTSS Project Was Not Adequately Planned, Initially Subject to DoIT Oversight, Nor Competitively Procured
findings.description: The LTSS IT project was not adequately planned nor was the required DoIT approval obtained when the project was initiated. DHMH's use of an MOU arrangement resulted in the project work not being subject to a competitive procurement as would normally be required by State procurement regulations.

dollar_amounts.context: Total project cost as of October 31, 2013

findings.recommendation: We recommend that DHMH ensure that, in the future, all information technology projects are properly planned; qualifying projects are submitted to DoIT for review and oversight prior to initiation; formal arrangements with state agencies are closely evaluated; and MOU provisions requiring review of subcontracts are complied with.

findings.title: Written Policies Were Not Established for Conducting Grant Audits Timely and in Accordance With Professional Standards
findings.description: The OIG had not established a formal written policy governing the timely completion of grant audits nor was there a policy to ensure the audits were conducted in accordance with established professional standards. Nine LHDs and 36 private providers had not been audited for at least five years.

dollar_amounts.context: LHD grant awards not audited for at least five years
Private provider grants not audited for at least five years

findings.recommendation: We recommend that the OIG establish a written policy to govern the timely completion of its grant audits; complete its grant audits on a timely basis; and establish a formal policy requiring LHD and private non-profit provider grant audits to be conducted in accordance with professional standards.

findings.title: Grantee Compliance with Sub-Vendor Audit and Oversight Requirements Were Not Verified During Grant Audits as Required
findings.description: The OIG did not adequately verify LHD and private non-profit provider compliance with sub-vendor audit and oversight requirements. For one LHD, the DOA had not verified adequate controls over its sub-vendors, and for two others, a listing of all sub-vendors was not obtained.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that the OIG properly verify LHD and private non-profit provider compliance with sub-vendor audit and oversight requirements during its audits of these entities in accordance with established DHMH standards.

findings.title: Records for Open Patient Financial Investigations Were Not Properly Maintained and Investigations Were Not Always Timely Conducted and Reviewed
findings.description: Records for open patient financial investigations were not properly maintained and monitored. According to a March 31, 2013 report, there were 185 patient accounts more than six months old where DCAR had not determined the amount due or billed for services.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that DHMH ensure that open patient financial investigation records are properly maintained and monitored, and financial investigations are timely conducted.

findings.title: Delinquent Accounts Receivable Were Not Adequately Pursued and Denied Insurance and Medicare Claims Were Not Timely Resolved
findings.description: Delinquent accounts receivable were not always adequately pursued for collection or transferred to the Department of Budget and Management's Central Collection Unit. Furthermore, claims which were originally denied by an insurance company or Medicare were not researched and timely resolved.

dollar_amounts.context: Denied claims not researched and timely resolved

findings.recommendation: We recommend that DHMH ensure delinquent accounts receivable are adequately pursued for collection and transferred to CCU as required; and denied insurance and Medicare claims are timely resolved.

findings.title: DCAR Lacked Appropriate Procedures to Ensure All Cash Receipts Were Deposited
findings.description: DCAR lacked appropriate procedures to ensure all cash receipts were deposited. The initial recordation documents were routed without ensuring a copy was forwarded directly to the employee responsible for verifying collections, and that employee had access to related collections.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that DHMH ensure the employee who prepares the initial record of collections forwards a copy directly to the deposit verification employee, and the deposit verification employee not have access to related cash receipts.

findings.title: Supervisory Oversight of Federal Fund Reimbursement Requests Was Not Always Effective
findings.description: Supervisory oversight of federal fund reimbursement requests could be improved. Reviews were not always effective as the accuracy of supporting schedules and memorandums were not always thoroughly verified.

dollar_amounts.context: Lost interest income due to delay in processing reimbursement request

findings.recommendation: We recommend that DHMH ensure that federal fund reimbursement requests are properly reviewed, along with supporting schedules and documents, and the reviews are documented.

findings.title: CPC Transactions Were Not Thoroughly Reviewed and Supported, Which Allowed Certain Improper Purchases to Go Undetected
findings.description: Corporate purchasing card transactions were not always thoroughly reviewed and supported. Our test disclosed purchases without itemized receipts and supervisory personnel did not always perform a documented review of Level-3 data.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that DHMH ensure all corporate card purchases are supported by appropriate documentation and thoroughly reviewed; activity logs and statements are signed as required; and Level-3 data is incorporated in supervisory review.

findings.title: Intrusion Detection Prevention System Coverage and Controls for the DHMH Network Were Insufficient
findings.description: Intrusion detection prevention system coverage and controls for the DHMH network were not sufficient. 130 servers within the neutral network zone were not protected by IDPS, and administrative access to the device was not adequately controlled.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that DHMH provide adequate IDPS coverage for all servers in the neutral network zone; limit network-level administrative access to the device; and ensure password and account controls comply with DoIT requirements.

findings.title: Network Access to Critical Internal Network Devices Was Not Properly Restricted and Monitoring of Certain Security Events Was Not Adequate
findings.description: Network access to critical internal network devices was not properly restricted. Numerous rules on firewalls allowed unnecessary access, and the device used to aggregate security logs was not configured to report security-related activities on the Internet firewall.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that DHMH configure its firewalls to properly protect all critical network devices; configure the aggregation device to include Internet firewall security-related activities; and review and analyze reports of Internet firewall activity.

findings.title: Malware Protection on DHMH Workstations and Servers Needs Improvement
findings.description: Malware protection on DHMH workstations and servers needs improvement. Anti-malware software was not properly configured to limit users' capabilities, outdated versions were running, and some computers lacked protection.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that DHMH disable settings allowing users to exclude files from malware scans; automatically update computers for latest anti-malware versions; limit administrative rights on user workstations; and ensure all computers are kept current for critical security-related updates.

findings.title: Controls Over the National Electronic Disease Surveillance System Database and the Hospital Management Information System Application Were Not Sufficient
findings.description: Controls over the NEDSS database and HMIS application were not sufficient. The NEDSS database was not configured to log security activity, passwords had no requirements for length or complexity, and critical security-related reports for HMIS were not reviewed.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that DHMH configure the NEDSS database to log all critical database security activity; ensure passwords comply with DoIT requirements; and review on a regular basis all HMIS critical security-related reports.

findings.title: Proper Controls Were Not Established Over the Processing of Settlement Checks Issued for Capital Grant Projects
findings.description: Proper internal controls were not established over the processing and handling of settlement checks issued for capital grant projects. One employee had unilateral control over the disbursement process, and OCP did not perform an independent verification.

dollar_amounts.context: Grant settlement checks returned for distribution during fiscal years 2012 and 2013

findings.recommendation: We recommend that DHMH establish adequate internal controls over capital project checks issued for grant projects, including proper authorization of payment requests, verification of check disposition by independent personnel, and reconciliation of expenditures.

findings.title: Record Keeping and Physical Inventory Procedures Were Not in Compliance with Certain DGS Requirements
findings.description: DHMH record keeping and physical inventory procedures were not in compliance with certain provisions of the Department of General Services' Inventory Control Manual. Equipment items purchased were not always recorded or tagged, and physical inventories were not certified.

dollar_amounts.context: Equipment items not properly recorded in detail records

findings.recommendation: We recommend that DHMH comply with the requirements of the Department of General Services' Inventory Control Manual.

extraction.agency_response_summary: The Administration generally concurred with the findings and recommendations. They did not concur with Finding 1 regarding the MERP procurement communication process but agreed to document risks in future procurements. For most other findings, they confirmed concurrence and outlined implementation steps or completed actions (e.g., March 2014 for security controls).
extraction.extraction_notes: Report date inferred as February 2015. Audit period extracted from Scope section. Prior findings count and repeated status derived from Status of Preceding Findings section.
